items.name: strict monoidal category
items.statement_summary: A strict monoidal category <B,box,e> is a category B with a bifunctor box:BxB->B that is strictly associative (box(box x 1) = box(1 x box), i.e. (a box b) box c = a box (b box c) on objects and arrows) and an object e that is a strict two-sided unit (box(e x 1) = id_B = box(1 x e), i.e. e box c = c = c box e and 1_e box f = f = f box 1_e). Being a bifunctor forces the interchange law 1_a box 1_b = 1_{a box b} and (f' box g')(f box g) = (f'f) box (g'g).

items.name: monoidal category (relaxed)
items.statement_summary: A monoidal category <B,box,e,alpha,lambda,rho> is a category B with a bifunctor box:BxB->B, a unit object e, and three natural isomorphisms: associator alpha_{a,b,c}: a box (b box c) ~= (a box b) box c, left unit lambda_a: e box a ~= a, right unit rho_a: a box e ~= a, subject to the pentagon coherence diagram (over four objects), the triangle diagram relating alpha,lambda,rho, and lambda_e = rho_e : e box e -> e. Associative and unital up to coherent natural isomorphism.

items.name: cartesian and cocartesian monoidal structure
items.statement_summary: Any category with finite products is monoidal: take a box b = a chosen binary product, e = a terminal object, and alpha,lambda,rho the unique isomorphisms commuting with the projections; the pentagon and triangle then commute automatically. Dually, any category with finite coproducts is monoidal with box = coproduct and e = an initial object.

items.name: tensor-product monoidal categories
items.statement_summary: Standard tensor products are monoidal categories: <Ab,tensor,Z> with associator forced by the universal property of the tensor product of abelian groups (universal among bilinear maps) and lambda:Z tensor A ~= A, rho:A tensor Z ~= A; likewise <K-Mod, tensor_K, K> for a commutative ring K, the category of K-algebras under tensor, graded and differential graded K-modules, and R-R bimodules under tensor_R.

items.name: strict morphism of monoidal categories
items.statement_summary: A strict morphism T:(B,box,e,alpha,lambda,rho)->(B',box',e',alpha',lambda',rho') is a functor T:B->B' strictly preserving the structure: T(a box b) = Ta box' Tb, T(f box g) = Tf box' Tg, Te = e', and T applied to alpha,lambda,rho equals alpha',lambda',rho' on components. Non-strict (relaxed) morphisms drop the alpha,lambda,rho conditions.

items.name: Moncat, the category of small monoidal categories
items.statement_summary: Moncat is the category of all small monoidal categories with strict morphisms as arrows; it has finite products, and the one-object monoidal category 1 (with its evident strict structure) is terminal. It contains a full subcategory of the strict monoidal categories.

items.name: Isbell: cannot strictify by identifying isomorphic objects
items.statement_summary: A monoidal category cannot be strictified merely by identifying all isomorphic objects (Isbell's argument): in the skeleton Set_0 of Set under x, a denumerable set D has D ~= DxD, and if the associator were the identity map compatible with the three projections one would derive f x (g x h) = (f x g) x h and, using p_1,p_2 epi, both f x g = f and f x g = g for all endomaps of D, an absurdity; similarly for the skeleton of <Ab,tensor>.

items.name: pentagon+triangle imply the secondary unit coherences
items.statement_summary: Prove that the pentagon (5) and triangle (7) imply the two derived unit-coherence diagrams (9); hint uses the pentagon at a=b=e and naturality to deduce (lambda box 1) alpha = lambda.

items.name: product in Moncat
items.statement_summary: Construct the product in Moncat of two monoidal categories.

items.name: opposite of a monoidal category is monoidal
items.statement_summary: For B monoidal, show that B^op carries the evident monoidal structure.

items.name: functor category is monoidal; exponential law is monoidal iso
items.statement_summary: For B monoidal and C any category, show the functor category B^C is monoidal with pointwise product (S box T)c = Sc box Tc and constant unit functor e:C->B, and that the adjunction/exponential B^{CxD} ~= (B^C)^D is an isomorphism of monoidal categories.

items.name: one-object strict monoidal category (Eckmann-Hilton)
items.statement_summary: Prove that a strict monoidal category with one object is a set (its arrows) equipped with two binary operations, composition and box, satisfying the interchange law and sharing a common two-sided unit id_e; cf. Exercise 5 of II.5.

items.name: independence of pentagon and triangle axioms
items.statement_summary: Show by examples that the pentagon axiom (5) and the triangle axiom (7) are independent.

items.name: binary word
items.statement_summary: Binary words (formal iterated products of a placeholder) defined by recursion: the length-0 word is e_0 (the empty word); the length-1 word is (-) (the placeholder/variable); if v,w are binary words of lengths m,n then v box w = (v) box (w) is a binary word of length m+n. These are the well-formed formal products with chosen parenthesization and specified e_0 slots.

items.name: the category W (free monoidal category on one generator)
items.statement_summary: W is the category whose objects are binary words and with exactly one arrow v->w between any two words of the same length (a preorder-groupoid: every arrow invertible and unique); it is a monoidal category under v,w |-> v box w with unit e_0 and with alpha,lambda,rho the unique such arrows. By construction every diagram in W commutes.

items.name: W is the free monoidal category on one generator
items.statement_summary: For any monoidal category B and any object b in B there is a unique morphism W->B of monoidal categories sending (-) |-> b (equivalently, substituting b into all blanks: (e_0)_b = e, (-)_b = b, (v box w)_b = v_b box w_b). Proof constructs the basic graph G_n of length-n words with basic alpha^{+-1} arrows, shows any two composite paths agree (associativity coherence), then folds in lambda,rho via G'_n.

items.name: coherence: canonical maps between word-functors
items.statement_summary: For a monoidal category B there is a function assigning to each pair of words v,w of the same length n a unique natural isomorphism can_B(v,w): v_B => w_B between the induced functors B^n->B (the canonical map), such that the identity e->e, the identity on the unit functor I_B, and alpha, alpha^{-1}, lambda, lambda^{-1}, rho, rho^{-1} are canonical, and canonical maps are closed under composite and under box-product. Consequently every diagram whose vertices are word-functors w_B and whose edges are built from 1, id, alpha, lambda, rho and their box-products commutes. Proof uses the auxiliary category It(B).

items.name: canonical maps between length-5 words (associahedron)
items.statement_summary: Draw the diagram of all canonical maps between binary words of length 5; it is a polyhedral subdivision of the sphere into 19 regions -- 16 pentagons (instances of alpha) and 3 squares (naturality).

items.name: Stasheff associahedron on the n-sphere
items.statement_summary: (Stasheff 1963) Show that the diagram of all canonical maps between words of length n+3 can be regarded as a polyhedral subdivision of the surface of the n-sphere (the associahedron).

items.name: free monoidal category on a set X
items.statement_summary: Construct the free monoidal category on any set X and prove its universal property; hint: objects are words with each x in X a length-1 word, with a surjection W_X -> M_X onto the free monoid on X, and a unique arrow v->w iff v,w have the same image in M_X.

items.name: monoid in a monoidal category
items.statement_summary: A monoid c in a monoidal category <B,box,e> is an object c with arrows mu: c box c -> c and eta: e -> c such that the associativity square (mu o (1 box mu) = mu o (mu box 1) o alpha : c box (c box c) -> c) and the two unit triangles (mu o (eta box 1) = lambda from e box c, and mu o (1 box eta) = rho from c box e) commute.

items.name: morphism of monoids
items.statement_summary: A morphism f: <c,mu,eta> -> <c',mu',eta'> of monoids is an arrow f: c -> c' with f mu = mu' (f box f) and f eta = eta'.

items.name: category Mon_B of monoids and its forgetful functor
items.statement_summary: The monoids in B and their morphisms form a category Mon_B, with a forgetful functor U: Mon_B -> B given by <c,mu,eta> |-> c.

items.name: monoids-in-B recover standard algebraic structures
items.statement_summary: Monoids in various monoidal categories specialize to familiar structures: in <Set,x,1> ordinary monoids; in <Top,x,*> topological monoids; in the endofunctor category <C^C,compose,Id> monads; in <Ab,tensor,Z> rings; in <K-Mod,tensor_K,K> K-algebras; graded modules give graded algebras; DG-K-Mod give differential graded K-algebras; in <B^op,box^op,e> comonoids in B; in <K-Mod^op,...> K-coalgebras; in <Cat,x,1> strict monoidal categories; in <O-Grph,x_O,O->O> categories.

items.name: General Associative Law for a monoid
items.statement_summary: (General Associative Law) For a monoid <c,mu,eta> in B, the iterated products mu_v, mu_w for any two words v,w of the same length n satisfy mu_w o can_c(v,w) = mu_v : v_c -> c, where can_c(v,w): v_c -> w_c is the canonical arrow of Theorem VII.2.1. Equivalently the n-fold product mu^{(n)}: c^n -> c is well defined and mu^{(n)}(mu^{(k1)} box ... box mu^{(kn)}) = mu^{(k1+...+kn)}. Proof: the monoid axioms are the alpha,lambda,rho cases, extended by induction over canonical maps.

items.name: construction of free monoids
items.statement_summary: If the monoidal category B has denumerable (countable) coproducts and every functor a box - and - box a preserves them, then the forgetful U: Mon_B -> B has a left adjoint; the free monoid on a is coproduct_n a^n (a^n the n-th box-power) with multiplication by juxtaposition a^m box a^n ~= a^{m+n} and unit the injection e = a^0 -> coproduct_n a^n. Specializes to: the free monoid on a set (B=Set), the tensor algebra sum_n A^n on a K-module (B=K-Mod), differential graded tensor algebras, and free topological monoids. Note: when a box - and - box a have right adjoints they automatically preserve coproducts.

items.name: Mon_B inherits finite products
items.statement_summary: Prove that if B has finite products then so does Mon_B.

items.name: coherence theorem for monoids
items.statement_summary: (Coherence for monoids) Interpret Proposition 1 (canonical maps mu_w) as a coherence theorem: in the graph with vertices the binary words and edges the arrows v_c -> w_c that are 1, mu, eta, instances of alpha, lambda, rho and their box-products, show any two paths w -> (-) have equal composite, but that this fails when the target is (-) box (-) of length 2.

items.name: substitution of words in a word
items.statement_summary: (Substitution of words) (a) Each word u of length n gives a functor u_W: W^n -> W; for words v_1,...,v_n the word u_W(v_1,...,v_n) has length the sum of the lengths of the v_i (substitute the v_i into u's n blanks). (b) For w = u_W(v_1,...,v_n) show the canonical maps satisfy mu_w = mu_u o (mu_{v1} box ... box mu_{vn}) o (appropriate canonical map), and that this generalizes Proposition 1.

items.name: left action of a monoid on an object
items.statement_summary: In a fixed monoidal category B, a left action of a monoid <c,mu,eta> on an object a in B is an arrow nu: c box a -> a such that the associativity square (nu o (1 box nu) = nu o (mu box 1) o alpha : c box (c box a) -> a) and the unit triangle (nu o (eta box 1) = lambda : e box a -> a) commute. Example: c acts on itself by mu (the left regular representation).

items.name: morphism of left actions
items.statement_summary: A morphism f: nu -> nu' of left c-actions is an arrow f: a -> a' with nu' o (1 box f) = f o nu : c box a -> a'.

items.name: category cLact of left actions with forgetful and free functors
items.statement_summary: Left c-actions and their morphisms form a category cLact; the forgetful functor cLact -> B (<nu: c box a -> a> |-> a) has a left adjoint b |-> c box b, whose action of c on c box b is the composite c box (c box b) -> (c box c) box b -> c box b via alpha and mu. This includes ordinary monoid-on-set actions, left R-modules, G-modules, and DG-algebra actions.

items.name: right action and bimodule
items.statement_summary: A right action of c on b is an arrow sigma: b box c -> b defined dually to a left action (associativity and unit compatibility); a commuting left-and-right action of c on a gives the analog of a bimodule (a two-sided module).

items.name: monad action on an endofunctor vs lifting to algebras
items.statement_summary: (Dubuc 1970) For a monad <T,eta,mu> in a category X, show that T has an action on an endofunctor S: X -> X iff S lifts to the category X^T of T-algebras as S = G^T S', and that such actions correspond one-to-one with the liftings S': X -> X^T.

items.name: strict monoidal category acting on a category
items.statement_summary: Let a small strict monoidal category B (a monoid in <Cat,x,...>) act on a category C; define the action of a monoid in B on an object of C, and use this to extend Exercise 1 to functors S: A -> X from any category A.

items.name: actions of a K-coalgebra
items.statement_summary: Describe the actions of a K-coalgebra (i.e. actions in the sense of this section when the monoid is a coalgebra / comonoid).

items.name: cLact inherits coproducts preserved by forgetful
items.statement_summary: If B has coproducts preserved by every functor a box -, show that cLact has coproducts and that the forgetful functor cLact -> B preserves them.

items.name: cLact inherits finite products
items.statement_summary: If the base category B has finite products, so does cLact, in such a way that the product projections a x a' -> a and a x a' -> a' (in B) become morphisms of actions in cLact.

items.name: tensor product of a right module by a left module
items.statement_summary: (Generalizing the tensor product of modules) If B has coequalizers, c is a monoid, sigma: b box c -> b a right action and nu: c box a -> a a left action, construct the tensor product b box_c a as the coequalizer of the two maps b box (c box a) => b box a given by the two actions, and prove that box_c is a functor Ract_c x cLact -> B.

items.name: coherence result for an action
items.statement_summary: (Coherence for an action) Given a left action nu: c box a -> a of a monoid c, describe the properties of the canonical maps nu_w: w_{c,a} -> a for words w of length >= 1 whose last argument is (-) (define this notion), where w_{c,a} results from substituting a for the last argument and c for all other arguments of w.

items.name: the simplicial category Delta and its universal monoid
items.statement_summary: Delta is the strict monoidal category whose objects are the finite ordinals n = {0,...,n-1} and whose arrows are the weakly monotone functions f: n -> n' (i <= j implies f i <= f j), with monoidal product ordinal addition +: Delta x Delta -> Delta (on objects n+m; on arrows, f+g places g beside f) and unit object 0; here 0 is initial and 1 is terminal. The unique arrows mu: 2 -> 1 and eta: 0 -> 1 make <1,mu,eta> a monoid in Delta, the universal monoid.

items.name: universal property of the simplicial category Delta
items.statement_summary: Given a monoid <c,mu',eta'> in a strict monoidal category <B,box,e>, there is a unique strict monoidal morphism F: <Delta,+,0> -> <B,box,e> with F1 = c, F mu = mu', F eta = eta'. Hence Delta's objects form the free monoid on 1 under +, and its arrows are generated by + and composition from mu: 2 -> 1 and eta: 0 -> 1 subject to the associative and unit laws; any arrow f: m -> n is a sum of iterated products mu^{(m_i)} of mu and eta.

items.name: coface maps and epi-mono factorization in Delta
items.statement_summary: Every monotone f: n -> n' factors as f = g o h with h surjective monotone and g injective monotone (g determined by its image, a subset of n'). The injective monotone maps n -> n+1 are the n+1 coface maps delta_i^n: n -> n+1 (i = 0,...,n) whose image omits i, i.e. delta_i^n{0,...,n-1} = {0,...,i-hat,...,n}. (The codegeneracies sigma_i, the unique-factorization Lemma, and the simplicial identities continue on printed page 177 / PDF 185, outside this range.)

items.name: unique normal-form (epi-mono) representation of arrows in Delta
items.statement_summary: In the simplicial category Delta, every arrow f : n -> n' factors uniquely as a composite of cofaces then codegeneracies, f = delta_{i_1} o ... o delta_{i_k} o sigma_{j_1} o ... o sigma_{j_h}, with n - h + k = n' and strictly decreasing/increasing subscript strings n' > i_1 > ... > i_k >= 0 and 0 <= j_1 < ... < j_h <= n-1. The proof derives the cosimplicial identities: (11) delta_i delta_j = delta_{j+1} delta_i for i<=j; (12) sigma_j sigma_i = sigma_i sigma_{j+1} for i<=j; (13) sigma_j delta_i = delta_i sigma_{j-1} (i<j), = 1 (i=j or i=j+1), = delta_{i-1} sigma_j (i>j+1).

items.name: generators and relations for Delta
items.statement_summary: The category Delta (objects all finite ordinals) is generated by the coface arrows delta_i^n : n -> n+1 and codegeneracy arrows sigma_j^n : n+1 -> n subject exactly to the cosimplicial relations (11), (12), and (13); i.e. Delta is presented by these generators and simplicial identities.

items.name: geometric-realization functor Delta -> Top (affine simplices)
items.statement_summary: A functor Delta : Delta -> Top exhibiting Delta as a subcategory of Top: the ordinal 0 goes to the empty space, and n+1 to the standard n-dimensional affine simplex {(t_0,...,t_n) in R^{n+1} : t_i >= 0, sum t_i = 1} (barycentric coordinates); an arrow f : n+1 -> m+1 goes to the affine map (t_0,...,t_n) |-> (s_0,...,s_m) with s_j = sum_{f i = j} t_i. Cofaces delta_i realize as the i-th face inclusion. (Verifying functoriality is left as an inline exercise.)

items.name: the subcategory Delta^+ of positive ordinals
items.statement_summary: Delta^+ denotes the full subcategory of Delta on the positive ordinals {1,2,3,...} (omitting only 0). Topologists relabel its objects by geometric dimension as {0,1,2,...} and call it Delta; Mac Lane retains the full Delta (which includes the ordinal 0) so that all face and degeneracy operations arise from the binary product mu and unit eta.

items.name: simplicial set
items.statement_summary: A simplicial set is a contravariant functor Delta^+ -> Set (equivalently a functor (Delta^+)^op -> Set).

items.name: simplicial object and its face/degeneracy description
items.statement_summary: A simplicial object in a category X is a functor S : (Delta^+)^op -> X; a morphism of simplicial objects is a natural transformation. Writing n+1 |-> S_n (object of n-simplices), delta_i |-> d_i, sigma_j |-> s_j, this is equivalently a sequence S_0, S_1, ... with face operators d_i : S_n -> S_{n-1} (i=0..n, n>0) and degeneracies s_i : S_n -> S_{n+1} (i=0..n, n>=0) satisfying the simplicial identities dual to (11)-(13): (11op) d_i d_{j+1} = d_j d_i for i<=j; (12op) s_i s_j = s_{j+1} s_i for i<=j; (13op) d_i s_j = s_{j-1} d_i (i<j), = 1 (i=j or i=j+1), = s_j d_{i-1} (i>j+1).

items.name: augmented simplicial object and augmentation
items.statement_summary: An augmented simplicial object in X is a functor S' : Delta^op -> X (over the full Delta, including 0). A simplicial object S is augmented by choosing an object S_{-1} and an arrow eps : S_0 -> S_{-1} with eps d_0 = eps d_1 : S_1 -> S_{-1} (so S'(delta_0) = eps); such eps is an augmentation of S.

items.name: homology of a simplicial object in an abelian category
items.statement_summary: For a simplicial object S in an abelian category A, the alternating sums d = d_0 - d_1 + ... + (-1)^{n+1} d_{n+1} : S_{n+1} -> S_n give a boundary with dd = 0 (from (11op)), making the sequence (15) S_0 <- S_1 <- S_2 <- ... a chain complex; its homology is H_0(S) = S_0/Im(d : S_1 -> S_0) and H_n(S) = Ker(d : S_n -> S_{n-1})/Im(d : S_{n+1} -> S_n) for n>0. An augmentation eps of S augments the complex (eps d = 0), giving H_0(S) -> S_{-1}.

items.name: singular chain complex and singular homology of a space
items.statement_summary: The composite functor Delta^op x Top --hom(Delta -, -)--> Set --Z--> Ab (Z = free abelian group on a set) assigns to each space X an augmented simplicial abelian group S(X): an arrow h in hom(Delta_{n+1}, X) is a singular n-simplex and S_{n+1} is the free abelian group on them. Its associated chain complex (via construction-homology) is the singular chain complex of X, with homology the singular homology of X.

items.name: four characterizations of Delta
items.statement_summary: Summary of the structural roles of Delta: (a) it is the category of finite ordinals, a full subcategory of Ord (all linearly ordered sets); (b) it is a full subcategory of Cat when each ordinal n is read as a finite preorder category (objects 0,1,2,...); (c) it is the strict monoidal category containing the universal monoid, its arrows being all iterated multiplications mu^{(m_0)} + ... + mu^{(m_{n-1})}; (d) it is a subcategory of Top consisting of the standard ordered simplices with order-preserving affine maps.

items.name: monic/epi in Delta = injective/surjective
items.statement_summary: Show that an arrow f : n -> n' in Delta is monic (resp. epi) if and only if the underlying monotone function f is injective (resp. surjective).

items.name: the monic subcategory Delta_mon
items.statement_summary: (a) Show the subcategory Delta_mon of all monics in Delta is generated by the coface arrows delta_i subject to the relations (11). (b) Show every arrow of Delta_mon is uniquely an iterated sum of eta : 0 -> 1 and id : 1 -> 1.

items.name: the epi subcategory Delta_epi and universal semigroup
items.statement_summary: (a) Show the subcategory Delta_epi of all epis in Delta is generated by the codegeneracy arrows sigma_i subject to the relations (12), and that Delta_epi is a strict monoidal category. (b) Defining a semigroup <c, mu> in a strict monoidal category <C, box, e> as an object c with an associative arrow mu : c box c -> c (mu(mu box 1) = mu(1 box mu)), show that 2 -> 1 is a universal semigroup in Delta_epi.

items.name: simplicial sets are small-complete
items.statement_summary: Show that the category of simplicial objects in Set is small-complete.

items.name: comonad (dual of monad)
items.statement_summary: A comonad L = <L, eps, delta> in a category A is an endofunctor L : A -> A with natural transformations eps : L -> Id_A (counit) and delta : L -> L^2 (comultiplication) satisfying coassociativity delta L . delta = L delta . delta : L -> L^3 and the counit laws eps L . delta = 1_L = L eps . delta : L -> L (equations (1)). Equivalently L is a comonoid in the strict monoidal category A^A of endofunctors under composition. This is the formal dual of the monad definition (VI.1).

items.name: comonads as augmented simplicial objects (dual universal property of Delta)
items.statement_summary: Delta contains the universal monoid <1, 0->1, 1+1->1>, so Delta^op contains the universal comonoid <1, 1->0, 1->1+1>. By the dual of Theorem 5.1, any comonad in a strict monoidal category <B, box, e> determines a unique monoidal morphism Delta^op -> B carrying the universal comonoid to it; this morphism is an augmented simplicial object in B (and (Delta^+)^op -> B is a simplicial object).

items.name: Smp L: the simplicial object of a comonad
items.statement_summary: A comonad <L, eps, delta> in A (a comonoid in A^A) determines an augmented simplicial object Smp L : Delta^op -> A^A with n |-> L^n = L o ... o L, augmentation eps, degeneracy delta = s_0 : L -> L^2, and higher faces/degeneracies (duals of (8),(9)) given by d_i^n = L^i eps L^{n-i} : L^{n+1} -> L^n (i=0..n) (2) and s_i^n = L^i delta L^{n-i-1} : L^n -> L^{n+1} (i=0..n-1) (3). Written Smp L = { L <= L^2 <= L^3 ... ; L -> L^2 => L^3 ... }.

items.name: comonad bar-resolution chain complex L^* a
items.statement_summary: If A is an Ab-category (e.g. abelian) and L a comonad, the simplicial identities make the alternating sums d = d_0 - d_1 + ... + (-1)^n d_n : L^{n+1} a -> L^n a satisfy dd = 0, giving a chain complex L^* a : L a <- L^2 a <- L^3 a <- ... with augmentation eps_a : L a -> a. This standard resolution of a is used to build derived functors and cohomology functors.

items.name: monoid-ring / group-ring functor Z : Mon -> Rng
items.statement_summary: The forgetful functor U : Rng -> Mon (forget addition) has (by the adjoint functor theorem) a left adjoint Z sending each monoid M to the monoid ring ZM. For a multiplicative group Pi, Z Pi is the group ring: its additive group is the free abelian group on Pi and its multiplication is the unique bilinear extension of the product of Pi.

items.name: free Pi-module functor Z(Pi) (x) - : Ab -> Pi-Mod
items.statement_summary: The forgetful functor U : Pi-Mod -> Ab has a left adjoint Z(Pi) (x) - sending an abelian group B to the Pi-module Z(Pi) (x) B. The unit is eta : B -> Z(Pi) (x) B, b |-> 1 (x) b, and the counit is eps : Z(Pi) (x) U A -> A, x (x) a |-> x a.

items.name: bar resolution of the trivial module Z (standard resolution for group (co)homology)
items.statement_summary: The composite Pi-Mod -> Ab -> Pi-Mod gives a comonad <L, eps, delta> with L = Z(Pi) (x) - and delta_A : L A -> L^2 A, x (x) a |-> x (x) 1 (x) a. Applying Smp L to the trivial module A = Z (x.m = m) yields, since Z(Pi) (x) Z = Z(Pi), the simplicial object Z(Pi) <= Z(Pi)^{(2)} <= ... <= Z(Pi)^{(n)} <= Z(Pi)^{(n+1)} ... where Z(Pi)^{(n)} is the n-fold tensor power, free abelian on bar symbols x[x_1|...|x_n], with Pi-action y.x[x_1|...|x_n] = yx[x_1|...|x_n], faces d_0 = x x_1[x_2|...], d_i = x[...|x_i x_{i+1}|...] (0<i<n), d_n = x[x_1|...|x_{n-1}], and degeneracies s_i inserting a 1. The associated augmented complex Z <- Z(Pi) <- Z(Pi)^{(2)} <- ... is the standard free resolution of the trivial Pi-module Z (Mac Lane 1963, Thm IV.5.1).

items.name: cohomology of a group H^n(Pi, A)
items.statement_summary: For a Pi-module A, applying hom_Pi(-, A) to the standard resolution (dropping the augmentation) yields a cochain complex hom_Pi(Z(Pi), A) -> hom_Pi(Z(Pi)^{(2)}, A) -> ... with coboundary delta = hom_Pi(d, A); its cohomology groups are the group cohomology H^n(Pi, A). Identifications: H^0(Pi, A) = {a : x a = a for all x} (invariants); H^1 = crossed homomorphisms Pi -> A modulo principal ones; H^2 = group extensions of the additive group A by Pi with the Pi-action given by conjugation.

items.name: homology of a group H_n(Pi, C)
items.statement_summary: For a right Pi-module C, applying the covariant additive functor C (x)_Pi - to the standard resolution and taking homology of the resulting complex in Ab gives the group homology H_n(Pi, C). Examples: H_0(Pi, Z) = Z and H_1(Pi, Z) = Pi/[Pi, Pi], the factor commutator (abelianization) of Pi.

items.name: symmetric monoidal category
items.statement_summary: A monoidal category B is symmetric when equipped with isomorphisms gamma_{a,b} : a box b ~= b box a natural in a, b, satisfying: gamma_{a,b} o gamma_{b,a} = 1 (1); the unit-compatibility rho_b = lambda_b o gamma_{b,e} : b box e ~= b (2); and the hexagon coherence diagram (3) relating gamma with the associator on a box (b box c). These conditions are exactly the symmetry axioms.

items.name: coherence for symmetric monoidal categories; product/coproduct are symmetric
items.statement_summary: The symmetry conditions suffice (Mac Lane 1963b) to prove that 'all' relevant diagrams commute, a coherence theorem analogous to that of section VII.2. Moreover any monoidal category whose tensor box is the categorical product or coproduct is automatically symmetric, taking gamma : a x b ~= b x a to be the canonical isomorphism commuting with the projections. (Elaborated in Chapter XI.)

items.name: closed category (symmetric monoidal closed)
items.statement_summary: A closed category V is a symmetric monoidal category in which each functor - box b : V -> V has a specified right adjoint (-)^b : V -> V (an internal hom functor). Examples: <Ab, (x)> is closed with A^B = hom(B, A); <K-Mod, (x)_K> for any commutative ring K; and the cartesian closed categories Set and Cat.

items.name: enriched category (B-category / V-category)
items.statement_summary: Relative to a monoidal category B, a B-category (V-category, category enriched over B) consists of a set R of objects, a hom-object R(r,s) in B for each pair, composition arrows R(s,t) box R(r,s) -> R(r,t), and unit arrows e -> R(r,r), subject to the usual associativity and unit axioms. This has only hom-objects, not hom-sets; applying a functor U : B -> Set (e.g. U = B(e, -)) to the hom-objects yields an ordinary underlying category U R 'enriched' by the R(r,s). The full theory works when B is closed, not merely monoidal.

items.name: compact-open function space and the local-compactness adjunction
items.statement_summary: Recalling the Set cartesian-closed adjunction Set(X x Y, Z) ~= Set(X, Z^Y) (1) via f |-> f^# with (f^# x) y = f(x,y), one topologizes Top(Y,Z) as Cop(Y,Z) with the compact-open topology (subbase N(C,U) = {continuous h : hC subset U} for C compact in Y, U open in Z). The exponential adjunction then restricts to a homeomorphism Top(X x Y, Z) ~= Top(X, Cop(Y,Z)) (2) provided Y is locally compact Hausdorff.

items.name: compactly generated space and the category CGHaus
items.statement_summary: A topological space X is compactly generated when every subset A of X that meets each compact subset C in a (relatively) closed set is itself closed. CGHaus denotes the category of compactly generated Hausdorff spaces (Kelley spaces) with all continuous functions as arrows.

items.name: CGHaus is coreflective in Haus
items.statement_summary: CGHaus is a full coreflective subcategory of Haus; the coreflection is witnessed by the Kelleyfication counit eps_Y : KY -> Y (universal from the inclusion's right adjoint K).

items.name: the Kelleyfication functor K : Haus -> CGHaus
items.statement_summary: For each Hausdorff space Y, KY has the same points, with A closed in KY iff A intersect C is closed in Y for every compact C subset Y. Then KY is compactly generated Hausdorff and the identity eps_Y : KY -> Y is continuous and universal from K, i.e. the counit of the coreflection (K is right adjoint to the inclusion CGHaus -> Haus). A map g : Y -> Z is continuous as g eps : KY -> Z iff g is continuous on all compact subsets of Y; metrizable and locally compact Hausdorff spaces are compactly generated.

items.name: CGHaus is complete and cocomplete
items.statement_summary: CGHaus is (small) complete and cocomplete. Completeness: Haus is complete and the right adjoint K preserves limits; in particular the product in CGHaus is the Kelleyfication box, X box Y = K(X x Y) (4), of the ordinary Haus product. Cocompleteness: coproducts (disjoint unions) of compactly generated spaces are compactly generated, and the coequalizer of a parallel pair, formed in Haus, already lies in CGHaus (shown via the K-counit being monic and iso onto the Haus coequalizer).

items.name: CGHaus is cartesian closed
items.statement_summary: CGHaus is a cartesian closed category. For compactly generated Hausdorff X, Y the exponential is X^Y = K(Cop(Y,X)) (5), the Kelleyfication of the compact-open function space, with evaluation e : X^Y box Y -> X, <f,y> |-> f y, shown continuous and universal, yielding the natural bijection CGHaus(Z box Y, X) ~= CGHaus(Z, X^Y) (6). One also gets the exponential-law homeomorphism X^{Z box Y} ~= (X^Y)^Z (7).

items.name: KY as colimit of compact subspaces
items.statement_summary: If Y is Hausdorff, show that KY is the colimit (in Haus) of the diagram of compact subspaces of Y ordered by inclusion.

items.name: closed/open subsets are compactly generated
items.statement_summary: Prove that a closed (or open) subset of a space X in CGHaus, with the usual subspace topology, is itself in CGHaus.

items.name: inclusion CGHaus -> Haus creates colimits
items.statement_summary: Prove that the inclusion functor CGHaus -> Haus creates colimits.

items.name: box-product agrees with x for locally compact factor
items.statement_summary: If Z is locally compact Hausdorff and X in CGHaus, prove that the CGHaus product Z box X equals the ordinary product Z x X.

items.name: alternative description of CGHaus
items.statement_summary: Prove that CGHaus is equivalent to the category whose objects are all Hausdorff spaces and whose arrows f : X -> Y are all functions that are continuous on compact sets.

items.name: pointed compactly generated spaces CGHaus_* and pointed function space
items.statement_summary: CGHaus_* is the category of pointed compactly generated Hausdorff spaces: objects are X in CGHaus with a chosen base point *_X, arrows are base-point-preserving continuous maps. The pointed function space X^{(*)Y} is the subspace of X^Y of base-point-preserving maps; being a closed subspace it is compactly generated, with base point the constant map Y -> *_X. The standard adjunction restricts to base-point-preserving transposes.

items.name: wedge, smash product, and the smash-hom adjunction
items.statement_summary: In CGHaus_*, the wedge is Z v Y = (Z box *) union (* box Y) inside Z box Y, and the smash product is the identification space Z ^ Y = (Z box Y)/[(Z box *) union (* box Y)] (collapsing the wedge to a point; also written Z # Y). Base-point-preserving maps out of Z box Y are exactly those collapsing the wedge, giving the adjunction CGHaus_*(Z ^ Y, X) ~= CGHaus_*(Z, X^{(*)Y}) (1); i.e. (- ^ Y) is left adjoint to (-)^{(*)Y}.

items.name: reduced suspension Sigma and loop space Omega with Sigma -| Omega
items.statement_summary: With the circle S^1 = I/{0,1} (base point 0 = +1), the reduced suspension and loop-space functors CGHaus_* -> CGHaus_* are Sigma X = X ^ S^1 and Omega X = X^{(*)S^1}; by the smash adjunction Sigma is left adjoint to Omega. Points of Omega X are based loops f : I -> X with f(0)=f(1)=*_X; Sigma X is the cylinder X x I with X x {0}, X x {1} and * x I collapsed (the double cone over X). Then Sigma^n S^1 is the (n+1)-sphere; the unit X -> Omega Sigma X sends x to the cone generator through x. By iteration Sigma^n is left adjoint to Omega^n, with unit X -> Omega^n Sigma^n X factoring as X -> Omega Sigma X -> ... , and Omega^n (a right adjoint) preserves products: Omega^n(X box Y) ~= Omega^n X box Omega^n Y.

items.name: left adjoint of Set_*(S, -)
items.statement_summary: Construct a left adjoint for the functor Set_*(S, -) : Set_* -> Set_* (on pointed sets).

items.name: smash makes CGHaus_* symmetric monoidal
items.statement_summary: Show that the smash product on CGHaus_* is commutative and associative up to natural isomorphisms making CGHaus_* a symmetric monoidal category whose unit is the two-point (pointed) space.

items.name: a functor in Top_* with no right adjoint
items.statement_summary: In Top_* (pointed spaces), show the cartesian-product functor - x Y has no right adjoint, because it fails to preserve coproducts. [operator recovered from PDF 198: it is x (categorical product), NOT the smash ^; smash by contrast IS closed.]

items.name: loop space as pullback of the path fibration
items.statement_summary: The path-space functor P (on pointed CG Hausdorff spaces) has PX = X^{(*)I} (with 0 the base point of I); f |-> f(1) defines a natural transformation pi : P -> Id. Show that Omega is obtained as the pullback of the diagram P -> Id <- * (the point). Classically Omega X is the fibre of pi_X : PX -> X.

items.name: counit of the Sigma-Omega adjunction
items.statement_summary: Describe the counit of the suspension-loop (Sigma -| Omega) adjunction.
